ideas.title: Chip a stone until it sings
ideas.critique: This is a real step for the knock project. The stone's shape becomes something the player edits, the modes are re-solved and you hear the result, so it isn't another 'knock and hear the notes' film. It stands or falls on the ear: the film has to let someone hear the pitch drop chip by chip, or it's just a rock losing voxels.

ideas.title: Soap bubbles with real film colours
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
same_form: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Light things drifting on the breeze is a shape the island has already filmed, and missed. The strong part is a thin-film material whose colour comes from the film's thickness, which a raster engine can't fake and the island has never shown. If the interference is done as a tinted look instead, all that's left is round dandelion puffs.

ideas.title: Writing with the sun
ideas.critique: Lasting marks and things that burn are both written in the goals, so this is expected however well it's made. What's strong is the caustic focused by the lens itself driving a heat equation in the wood, so the spot size really depends on how the glass is held.

ideas.title: Sky lanterns
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
same_form: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A flock of small lights drifting on the wind at dusk repeats the dandelion and firefly films with a buoyancy formula added. The ideal-gas 'is it ready yet' moment is a decent mechanic, but you get it once, and the film is warm dots floating out to sea.

ideas.title: Dam the stream
ideas.critique: A GPU shallow-water field over real terrain is something new to play with: water that backs up, overflows and finds its own way gives emergent results every time. The risk is the plainest version, a blue sheet sliding downhill with no stream for the stones to meet. Water also sits close to what the goals name.

ideas.title: Footprints in mud
ideas.critique: Ground you can deform is a real engine capability the island lacks. But the payoff, a trail worn into the ground that you can follow, is the one the ant films just had, and prints filling with water reads as decal work unless the soil model really shows.

ideas.title: Fold a paper plane
same_form: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: It reuses paperpage.jl and has the same recipe as the boomerang: one thrown object whose flight path the physics draws. The camera follows the arc again. Trimming the tail until it glides is a good loop, but a viewer has seen this film twice already.

ideas.title: Fell a tree
ideas.critique: A hinge that bends before it breaks and steers the fall is a nice mechanism. Things that fall and break are named in the goals, though, and the likely version is a rigid cylinder tipping over a joint, with the fibre-direction wood claimed in the pitch but nowhere to be seen.

ideas.title: Sand castles the tide takes
ideas.critique: Granular matter whose cohesion depends on wetness would be a new kind of material on the island, and a time-lapse of walls slumping can be watched again. It's very ambitious for a session, and the likely result is a heightmap that erodes, which loses the dry-slides, wet-stands contrast that makes it worth making.

ideas.title: A rope swing over the pond
ideas.critique: Pumping a pendulum and timing the release is a good, repeatable skill toy. But a verlet rope and a ballistic arc are textbook, and the 'real splash' is where it will most likely be faked. The film is one swing and one splash, close to the island's other single-throw shots.
